description: Linguistic analysis of text: tokenization into words and sentences, frequency counting, entity and structure extraction, language identification and translation, stemming and stopword removal, dictionary lookup, and string similarity and alignment measures.

tools.name: TextWords
tools.description: Splits text into a list of words, handling punctuation and language-specific rules. An optional count returns only the first n words. It is the standard tokenizer for word-level analysis.
tools.example: TextWords["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."]
tools.notes: TextCases with "Word" gives positions and structure; StringSplit is the lower-level alternative.

tools.name: TextSentences
tools.description: Splits text into sentences, correctly handling abbreviations, decimals and quotation. It is much more reliable than splitting on periods. Use it as the first step for sentence-level analysis or summarization.
tools.example: TextSentences["Dr. Smith arrived at 3.5 km. He left soon after."]

tools.name: WordCounts
tools.description: Returns an association of word frequencies in a text, sorted by count. A second argument limits the result to the n most common words, and a third can restrict to specific word types. It is the fastest route to a frequency profile.

tools.name: WordFrequency
tools.description: Gives the relative frequency of specified words within a text, as fractions of the total word count. It accepts patterns as well as literal words. Use it to compare usage rates across texts of different lengths.

tools.name: TextCases
tools.description: Extracts fragments of text matching a specified linguistic category, such as a named entity type, part of speech or structural unit. Categories include "Person", "Country", "Date", "Number", "Noun" and many more. Use it as the main named-entity and pattern extraction tool.
tools.example:
TextCases["Ada Lovelace was born in London in 1815.",
  {"Person", "City", "Date"}]
tools.notes: TextPosition gives the character ranges of the same matches; TextContents returns a structured Dataset.

tools.name: TextContents
tools.description: Returns a Dataset of all recognized content elements in a text, with their type, string, position and interpretation. It gives a structured overview rather than a filtered list. Use it to explore what a document contains before writing targeted extraction.
tools.example: TextContents["Marie Curie worked in Paris and won the Nobel Prize in 1903."]

tools.name: TextStructure
tools.description: Analyzes the grammatical structure of text, returning constituent trees, part-of-speech assignments or dependency information. The form of output is selected by the second argument. Use it for syntactic analysis and linguistic teaching examples.
tools.example: TextStructure["The cat sat on the mat.", "WordTypes"]

tools.name: TextPosition
tools.description: Returns the character positions of text fragments matching a given linguistic type or string pattern. It complements TextCases, which returns the fragments themselves. Use it for highlighting and in-place editing.

tools.name: LanguageIdentify
tools.description: Identifies the natural language of a text, returning an Entity or a ranked list of candidates with probabilities. Short texts can be ambiguous, so probabilities are useful. Use it to route text to language-specific processing.
tools.example: LanguageIdentify[{"Bonjour tout le monde", "Guten Morgen", "Buenos dias"}]

tools.name: TextTranslation
tools.description: Translates text into a target language, detecting the source language automatically when not given. It uses an external translation service. Use it for multilingual pipelines and quick translations inside computations.
tools.notes: Requires an internet connection and service access.

tools.name: WordTranslation
tools.description: Translates individual words, returning possible translations rather than a single sentence-level rendering. It draws on dictionary data instead of a translation service. Use it for vocabulary work and word-by-word glossing.

tools.name: DeleteStopwords
tools.description: Removes common function words such as "the", "of" and "and" from text or from a list of words. A custom stopword list can be supplied. Use it before frequency analysis, word clouds and topic modelling.
tools.example: DeleteStopwords["the analysis of the results of the experiment"]

tools.name: WordStem
tools.description: Reduces a word to its stem, so that inflected forms map together. It applies a rule-based stemming algorithm rather than a dictionary lookup. Use it to group related word forms before counting.

tools.name: Pluralize
tools.description: Returns the plural form of an English word or phrase, handling irregular forms. Given a number it produces the correctly agreeing phrase. Use it for generated report text and user-facing messages.

tools.name: Alphabet
tools.description: Returns the alphabet of a specified language or script as a list of characters. Types such as "Vowels" or "Consonants" select subsets. Use it for cipher work, puzzles and linguistic computations.

tools.name: WordList
tools.description: Returns a list of common words of a given type and language, such as all known nouns or a basic vocabulary. It is useful as a vocabulary source for filtering and generation. Types include "KnownWords", "CommonWords", "Stopwords" and part-of-speech names.

tools.name: RandomWord
tools.description: Returns one or more randomly chosen dictionary words, optionally restricted by type or language. It is convenient for generating test data, passphrases and examples. Definitions can be requested at the same time.

tools.name: DictionaryWordQ
tools.description: Tests whether a string is a word in a dictionary, in English by default. Language and case handling are options. Use it for spell checking, word games and input validation.

tools.name: SpellingCorrectionList
tools.description: Returns a ranked list of plausible spelling corrections for a word. Candidates are drawn from the dictionary using edit distance and frequency. Use it to suggest alternatives for misspelled input.

tools.name: WordDefinition
tools.description: Returns the dictionary definitions of a word, grouped by part of speech. It is the quick-lookup counterpart of WordData["word", "Definitions"]. Use it for glossaries and vocabulary tools.

tools.name: EditDistance
tools.description: Computes the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings or lists, the minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions needed to transform one into the other. It is the standard measure of string similarity. Use it for fuzzy matching and spell checking.
tools.usage:
EditDistance[s1, s2]
EditDistance[s1, s2, IgnoreCase -> True]
tools.notes: DamerauLevenshteinDistance also counts transpositions, which better models typing errors.

tools.name: DamerauLevenshteinDistance
tools.description: Computes edit distance allowing transposition of adjacent characters as a single operation. It models common keyboard typos more accurately than plain Levenshtein distance. Use it for search-as-you-type and data deduplication.

tools.name: HammingDistance
tools.description: Counts the number of positions at which two equal-length strings or lists differ. It is the natural metric for fixed-length codes and binary vectors. Use it for error-correcting codes and bit-level comparison.

tools.name: SmithWatermanSimilarity
tools.description: Computes local sequence alignment similarity between two strings or lists using the Smith-Waterman algorithm. It finds the best-matching subsequences rather than aligning the whole inputs. Use it for biological sequences and partial string matching.
tools.notes: NeedlemanWunschSimilarity performs global rather than local alignment.

tools.name: LongestCommonSubsequence
tools.description: Finds the longest subsequence common to two strings or lists, allowing gaps. It underlies diff algorithms and similarity measures. Use it to compare document versions and sequences.
tools.notes: LongestCommonSubsequencePositions returns where the matches occur; LongestCommonSequence requires contiguity.

tools.name: SequenceAlignment
tools.description: Aligns two strings or lists and returns their common and differing parts in order, effectively a diff. Matching segments appear directly and differences as pairs of alternatives. Use it for change tracking and sequence comparison.
tools.usage:
SequenceAlignment[a, b]
SequenceAlignment[a, b, SimilarityRules -> rules]
tools.example: SequenceAlignment["the quick brown fox", "the quiet brown cat"]

tools.name: TextSearch
tools.description: Searches files, directories or search indexes for text matching a query, returning the matching items ranked by relevance. It supports boolean queries, proximity and fuzzy matching. Use it for full-text search over document collections.
tools.notes: CreateSearchIndex builds a persistent index; TextSearchReport gives scores and highlighted snippets.

tools.name: CreateSearchIndex
tools.description: Builds a persistent full-text search index over files, strings or a Dataset. Indexing once makes repeated searches fast. Use it for document repositories and knowledge bases.
tools.example:
idx = CreateSearchIndex[{"alpha beta gamma", "beta delta"}];
TextSearch[idx, "beta"]

tools.name: Snippet
tools.description: Extracts a short excerpt from a long text, optionally centered on a search term. It is useful for previews and search result summaries. The length is given in lines or words.
